headline: AI-driven optical demand fuels a ninth quarter of growth
summary_short: Corning's Q2 2026 GAAP revenue rose to $4.51B (+16.7% y/y), net income climbed to $559M (+19.2% y/y) and diluted EPS reached $0.64 (+18.5% y/y), while core (non-GAAP) EPS grew 30% to $0.78 on strength in Optical Communications.
summary_long: Optical Communications sales rose 32% y/y to $2.07B, led by a 65% jump in Enterprise Networks and accelerating Gen AI product demand, powering consolidated revenue and operating income (+21.8% y/y) as opex grew slower than gross profit. Solar swung to a $7M net loss (from $2M income) on an extended maintenance shutdown and equipment upgrade at its wafer facility; management expects improved Solar profitability in Q3. Cash rose to $2.50B from $1.53B at year-end. For Q3 2026, Corning guided core sales to $4.9B-$5.0B (~16% y/y) and core EPS to $0.85-$0.89 (~28% y/y), and reiterated its recently upgraded Springboard Plan targeting a $20B annualized sales run rate by end-2026, rising to $30B by end-2028 and $40B by end-2030.

drivers.explanation: Optical Communications sales rose 32% y/y to $2.07B, including a 65% increase in Enterprise Networks, with Gen AI product sales growing significantly faster — the primary engine of consolidated revenue growth.

GAAP gross margin held roughly flat (36.1% vs 36.0% y/y) as cost of sales grew 16.5%, nearly matching revenue's 16.6% growth; core gross margin, which excludes hedging and one-off items, expanded 120bp to 39.6%.
Operating margin expanded to 15.5% from 14.8% y/y as total operating expenses (SG&A + R&D + amortization, $930M) grew 13.6%, slower than gross profit's 17.0% growth.

Tracks the same segment growth as operating income, net of non-operating items on the income statement (interest income $12M, translated-earnings-contract gain $90M, interest expense $94M, other expense $57M); Yahoo's EBIT figure does not tie exactly to a single GAAP subtotal in the release.
Adds back depreciation and amortization of $391M (vs $340M y/y) to EBIT; as with EBIT, the shard's EBITDA figure does not tie exactly to a single GAAP subtotal disclosed in the release.

Broad-based segment growth, led by Optical Communications net income +77% y/y to $438M, drove the increase, partially offset by swings to losses at Solar (-$7M from +$2M) and Life Sciences (-$21M from +$6M).
Tracks the net-income growth above; diluted weighted-average shares rose slightly to 875M from 865M y/y, a modest drag versus the net-income growth rate.

CEO Wendell Weeks attributed results to the recently upgraded Springboard Plan and new customer partnerships with Amazon and NVIDIA expanding U.S. optical manufacturing capacity; Solar's net loss was attributed to an extended maintenance shutdown and equipment upgrade at the solar wafer facility, with profitability expected to improve in Q3.
